chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz ibn Abdillah from Zurarah who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who made up a day of fasting from the month of Ramadan, and then had intercourse with his wife. He said: 'Upon him is from the expiation what is upon the one who had intercourse in the month of Ramadan, on that day in the sight of Allah from the days of Ramadan.'

This report came rarely, and it can be intended for the one who broke his fast on that day after midday, in a manner of slighting and minimizing what is obligatory upon him from the command of Allah, the Exalted. Thus, at that time, the expiation obligatory upon him is what is upon the one who breaks his fast for a day in the month of Ramadan, as a punishment and severity upon him. As for the one who breaks his fast while believing that it is preferable to complete his fasting, then upon him is only what we have previously mentioned: feeding ten poor people or fasting three days.
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for intercourse during a makeup day of Ramadan fasting?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this rare narration from Zurarah, where Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that breaking a makeup fast via intercourse incurs the same expiation as breaking a Ramadan fast, provided the act was done with slighting of the obligation. The commentary distinguishes this from cases where one breaks the fast while believing completion is preferable, which requires only feeding ten poor or fasting three days, highlighting the Shia juristic nuance between intent and ritual status.
